newsitem.title: CHINA: China names lawmakers for post-1997 Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China names lawmakers for post-1997 Hong Kong.

text.p: China founded a Provisional Legislature on Saturday to take over lawmaking in Hong Kong when the British colony reverts to Beijing's sovereignty at midnight on June 30 next year.
The following is a list showing the composition of the new body, grouped according to affiliations. The political groups named are all pro-Beijing organisations.
Liberal Party (10)
- Allen Lee, Selina Chow, Ronald Arculli, Howard Young,
Lau Wong-fat, James Tien, Edward Ho, Ngai Siu-kit,
Miriam Lau, Henry Tang.
Democratic Alliance for the Betterment of Hong Kong (7)
- Tsang Yok-sing, Tam Yiu-chung, Cheng Kai-nam,
Ngan Kam-chuen, Cheung Hon-chung,
Chan Kam-lam, Ip Kowk-him.
Federation of Trade Unions (3)
- Cheng Yiu-tong, Chan Yuen-han (DAB), Chan Wing-chan (DAB)
Progressive Alliance (5)
- Tso Wong Man-yin, Ambrose Lau, Choy Kan-pui,
Tang Siu-tong, Yeung Yiu-chung
Liberal Democratic Foundation (3)
- Wong Siu-yee, Maria Tam, David Chu.
New Hong Kong Alliance (2)
- Philip Wong, Kan Fook-yee
Civil Force (1)
- Lau Kong-wah
Association for Democratic and People's Livelihood (4)
- Frederick Fung, Mok Ying-fan, Bruce Liu, Law Cheung-kwok
Independents (24)
- David Li, Ho Sai-chu, Lee Kai-ming, Wu King-cheong,
Hui Ying-fat, Yu Sun, Paul Cheng, Lo Suk-ching,
Ho Chun-tai, Ma Fung-kwok, Andrew Wong, Leung Chun-ying,
Elsie Tu, Ng Leung-sing, Rita Fan, Yuan Wu,
Leong Che-hung, Chim Pui-chung, Timothy Fok, Eric Li,
Ng Ching-fai, Peggy Lam, Leung Lau Yau-fun, Wong Ying-ho.
Former Democratic Party member (1)
- Dominic Chan
